Aliases_in_paper: P. falciparum apicoplast calcium binding protein 1

GeneSummary.bullet_point: MAL13P1.156 is a single exon gene (1599 bp) encoding a 64 kDa protein that contains an EF-hand calcium binding domain (prediction e-value 2.80E-13) at positions 234-518 amino acids, with a signal anchor (probability 0.954) and apicoplast targeting peptide at its C-terminus (5 of 5 positive tests).
supporting_quotes: MAL13P1.156 is a single exon gene (1599 bp) that codes for a 64 kDa protein and contains an EF-hand domain (prediction e-value, 2.80E −13) at the position between 234 and 518 amino acid of the deduced polypeptide.
MAL13P1.156, a calcium binding protein that contain a signal anchor with probability of 0.954 and 5 of 5 positive tests for an apicoplast targeting peptide at its C-terminus.

GeneSummary.bullet_point: The protein localizes to the apicoplast, as demonstrated by immunofluorescence microscopy showing characteristic apicoplast patterns (single small compartment in early schizonts, elongated branched formation in late schizonts, and divided punctuate formations in daughter merozoites) and partial colocalization with apicoplast marker EF-Tu.
supporting_quotes: immunofluorescence microscopy (IFA) of the transgenic cell line using the anti-GFP antibody shows the characteristic pattern of apicoplast localization with a single small compartment in the early schizonts, elongated branched formation in the late schizonts, and finally divided punctuate formations corresponding to new apicoplast precursors in the newly formed daughter merozoites
Finally there is partial but significant colocalization between MAL13P1.156 and the apicoplast marker EF-Tu

GeneSummary.bullet_point: Western blot analysis of the MAL13P1.156-GFP fusion protein shows expression as a full-length 91 kDa protein (64 kDa + 27 kDa GFP) and a processed form of ~72 kDa, consistent with signal peptide cleavage upon import to the apicoplast.
supporting_quotes: Western blot analyses show a strong expression of this protein as a full-length fusion protein of 91 kDa (64 kDa full-length protein plus 27 kDa GFP) and a processed form ~72 kDa
This proteolytic cleavage is consistent with the signal peptide processing upon import to the apicoplast.

GeneSummary.bullet_point: Overexpression of MAL13P1.156 (renamed PfACBP1) increases parasite resistance to ionomycin by approximately 2-fold (P value 0.01) at 0.5 μM ionomycin concentration, with survival rates comparable to non-transfected parasites grown in medium supplemented with 500 μM CaCl2.
supporting_quotes: At 0.5 μM of ionomycin (that roughly corresponds to the ionomycin IC50; see below), the survival of the PfACBP1 overexpressing cell line is ~2-fold higher (P value 0.01) compared to the nontransfected parasites
The survival rate of the transgenic cell line is comparable to the nontransfected parasites grown in the medium supplemented with 500 μM of CaCl2.

GeneSummary.bullet_point: The protein shows structural homology to several calcium binding proteins including EF-hand calcium binding protein from Entamoeba histolytica (E-value 0.002), CDPK3 from Cryptosporidium parvum (E-value 0.053), myristoylated NCS1p from Schizosaccharomyces pombe (E-value 0.10), and CDPK-1 from Toxoplasma gondii (E-value 0.35), with considerable conservation of the calcium binding domain.
supporting_quotes: A search of the RCSB Protein Data Bank (PDB) for structurally similar proteins retrieved several sequences of calcium binding proteins with the EF-hand calcium binding domain. These include an EF-hand calcium binding protein from Entamoeba histolytica (E-value 0.002, solution NMR), CDPK3 (calcium-dependent protein kinase-3) from Cryptosporidium parvum (E-value 0.053, X-ray diffraction), myristoylated NCS1p from Schizosaccharomyces pombe (E-value 0.10, solution NMR) and CDPK-1 (calcium-dependent protein kinase-1) from Toxoplasma gondii (E-value 0.35, X-ray diffraction).
Multiple alignments of the amino acids spanning the EF-hand domain (214th to 341th positions) show considerable conservation of the calcium binding domain between these structural homologues

GeneSummary.bullet_point: MAL13P1.156 was identified through bioinformatics analysis of all 545 plastid-targeted nuclear encoded proteins and showed the highest homology to the EF-hand consensus sequence among apicoplast-targeted proteins.
GeneSummary.evidence_location: Results section 2.3, paragraph 1; Discussion section, paragraph 4
supporting_quotes: For this we carried out bioinformatics analyses of all 545 plastid targeted nuclear encoded proteins and identified MAL13P1.156, a calcium binding protein

In our bioinformatics analyses of the 545 plastid targeted proteins, PfACBP1 showed the highest homology to the EF-hand consensus sequence which suggests its crucial role in calcium-mediated regulatory function(s) in this compartment.

AdditionalInferences: The increased ionomycin resistance conferred by PfACBP1 overexpression suggests the protein functions to retain calcium concentration in the apicoplast through its calcium binding properties, supporting a role in apicoplast calcium homeostasis.
The protein likely functions in calcium-dependent signaling within the apicoplast, potentially involved in sensing and/or buffering free Ca2+ ions similar to plant chloroplast counterparts.

PfACBP1 may play a role in regulating apicoplast gene expression through calcium-mediated mechanisms, given the observed effects of calcium ionophores on apicoplast transcription and the protein's calcium-binding properties.

The close proximity between MAL13P1.156-labeled compartments and mitochondria (labeled by mitotracker Red) is consistent with the known physical association between apicoplast and mitochondria in P. falciparum.
The protein represents a potential component of calcium-dependent regulatory mechanisms in the apicoplast, which could be explored as a drug target for liver stage malaria treatment.
data.ShortSummary: MAL13P1.156 (PfACBP1) is a 64 kDa apicoplast-targeted calcium binding protein containing an EF-hand domain that localizes to the apicoplast and whose overexpression confers 2-fold increased resistance to ionomycin, suggesting a crucial role in apicoplast calcium homeostasis and signaling.
